title: Write the sandbox threat model and security design doc (GATE)
description:
Nothing else in the sandbox track may start until this is written and reviewed. The user explicitly asked for code execution to be carefully examined security-wise.

Must cover, concretely:
- Why in-process execution is unacceptable: chat-backend runs as ROOT (suite docs/project-spec.md:362 - it raises ulimit and owns root-owned chat-data PVC files), and ENABLE_SCRIPT_EXECUTION is false in production today. sandbox_tools.py:21 _ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS is an allow-list precisely because a deny-list previously leaked INTERNAL_API_SECRET.
- Isolation boundary: separate pod, non-root, read-only rootfs, drop ALL capabilities, RuntimeDefault or stricter seccomp, no shell, gVisor/sandboxed-node evaluation, memory/CPU/pid limits, wall-clock timeout, output size caps.
- Egress: deny by default. The sandbox reaches db-api and results-api ONLY, never the internet, never the chat-data PVC, never the Keycloak/postgres services.
- Credentials: the sandbox must NOT hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. Design a short-lived per-request scoped token. Note the precedent problem at suite docs/project-spec.md:237 - mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api NetworkPolicy, so a NetworkPolicy alone is not a boundary.
- MCP exposure: per explicit user requirement, code execution must NOT be reachable via /mcp. Enumerate every layer enforcing this (tool registration, NetworkPolicy, and a test).
- Abuse cases: crypto mining, data exfiltration via db-api, resource exhaustion starving chat-backend on a shared node, prompt-injected scripts from user-supplied attachments or tool results.

Deliverable: docs/code-execution-security.md in genetics-results-suite, plus a new documentation-ownership row in CLAUDE.md.
close_reason:
Design of record written: docs/code-execution-security.md (892 lines), plus a CLAUDE.md documentation-ownership row and the docs/ tree entry in project-spec.md. Committed 6f7f520.

Two reviewers (codebase-accuracy + adversarial security), two fix rounds. Round 1's fixes introduced two new breaks which round 2 closed; stopped at two rounds per policy rather than a third.

WHAT REVIEW CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE WOULD HAVE:
- The central isolation claim was unsound. Dedicated KSA with no Workload Identity binding only holds under GKE_METADATA node mode; a pool built from the first spec would default to GCE_METADATA + the Compute default SA, exposing the raw metadata server. GKE_METADATA needs cluster-level WI, which gke.tf gates on manage_iam, so it fails at APPLY not plan - and the cheap escape re-introduces the hole.
- results-api accepts a forged X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email from any namespace pod (from-less ingress rule + header fallback). Filed as genetics-results-suite-fad; .8/.9 blocked on it.
- Routing JWTs by dot-count would have 401'd every Google Identity Token. Now discriminates on the JOSE alg header.
- Pod-level /tmp emptyDir was a sequential cross-conversation channel; concurrency 1 bounds concurrent leakage, not sequential.
- read_artifact reusing SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS (=/data) would have handed the model a read primitive over chat_history.db and llm_config.db.
- The db-api ingress policy admits only chat-backend and mcp-server, so the sandbox egress allow-list alone left the primary data path dead. Both reviewers found this independently.
- The TOOL_PROFILE argument for MCP exclusion was backwards: mcp-server passes no profile, tool_profile=None means NO filtering, so _mcp_disabled membership is the sole registration-layer control.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE TICKET:
- DNS eliminated (hostAliases as v1 default) rather than allowed with tunnelling booked as residual. Rationale: ~200 KB/s sustained exfiltration falsified two load-bearing controls. Reversible - the doc carries an explicit revert clause. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS.
- gVisor on a separate pinned 1-node pool. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS EITHER; it is a permanent extra node.

LEFT UNDONE: wording/stale-count/citation drift batched as genetics-results-suite-5r2. The doc's node-pool sizing assumes a pinning that is not actually in effect - genetics-results-suite-262 blocks .10.

CAVEAT FOR IMPLEMENTERS: 892 lines of design that has never met an implementation. Expect .6/.7 to find over-specification; prefer amending the doc over silently diverging.

title: Five by-gene BigQuery MCP tools emit unlabeled rows and their download link raises
description:
Found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07, verified independently. PRE-EXISTING - the SDK work did not cause it.

db-api returns query rows POSITIONALLY, not as dicts: genetics-results-db/api/main.py:579 builds rows.append([_serialize_value(v) for v in row.values()]) and column names travel separately in a 'columns' key (main.py declares rows: list[list[Any]]).

Five executor methods take result.get('rows', []) and pass it on without ever carrying 'columns':
  executor.py:910   get_asm_qtl_by_gene            -> {gene}_asm_qtl.tsv
  executor.py:1053  get_open_chromatin_by_gene     -> {gene}_open_chromatin.tsv
  executor.py:1114  get_variant_effect_by_gene     -> {gene}_variant_effect.tsv
  executor.py:1193  get_mpra_by_gene               -> {gene}_mpra.tsv
  executor.py:1251  get_mpra_pip_concordance_by_gene -> {gene}_mpra_pip_concordance.tsv

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both live today:

1. The MODEL receives 'results': [[...], [...]] - bare positional lists with no column names. It has to guess which value is which column, for five tools covering ASM-QTL, open chromatin, variant effect and MPRA by gene.

2. The DOWNLOAD RAISES. Those five set _download_data = {'results': <list of lists>}, and llm_service.py _convert_to_tsv takes the 'results' branch, which does headers = list(results[0].keys()) - AttributeError on a list. The 'columns'/'rows' branch immediately above it would have worked, but these five do not populate it.

Note the other ~20 _download_data sites pass genuine list-of-dicts and are fine. Only the five BigQuery-backed by-gene tools are affected - they are the ones that go through query_database rather than results-api.

RECOMMENDED FIX (one change fixes the model surface, the download, and the SDK together): in those five methods, zip 'columns' with each row to build list-of-dicts before putting it in 'results'. That changes the MCP payload shape from list-of-lists to list-of-dicts for these five tools - which is why it needs a decision rather than being folded into .11 silently. The current shape is broken, so this is a bug fix rather than a behaviour change, but it does alter what the model sees.

genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 works around it on the SDK side only, leaving the MCP surface as-is.

title: results-api trusts a forgeable identity header from any pod in the namespace
description:
Found by adversarial security review of the sandbox design (genetics-results-suite-4h6.5), verified independently 2026-08-07.

TWO pre-existing facts combine into an authentication bypass:

1. genetics-results-api/app/core/auth.py get_verified_user() falls back to get_authenticated_user() when no Authorization header is present. get_authenticated_user (line 30-36) reads the raw X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email header and does nothing but split it on ':'. There is no validation that the request came from auth-gateway.

2. k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml allow-ingress-results-api contains a rule with ports but NO from clause:
     ingress:
     - ports:
       - port: 4000
   A from-less rule admits ALL sources. So results-api on 4000 is reachable from any pod in the genetics namespace, bypassing auth-gateway entirely.

results-api runs REQUIRE_AUTH=true, so auth is genuinely enforced - which is exactly why the fallback matters. auth-gateway does handle the header correctly at the edge (blanks it at auth-gateway.yaml:120, sets it from the verified oauth2-proxy email at 145/163/178/210), so EXTERNAL traffic is safe. The hole is namespace-internal.

CURRENT SEVERITY: latent. Every pod in the namespace today runs trusted first-party code, so nothing exploits it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the code-execution sandbox (epic genetics-results-suite-4h6) puts LLM-authored, prompt-injectable code inside that namespace with results-api as an ALLOWED egress destination. That converts this latent hole into an exploited one: a script can skip its scoped token entirely, send X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email: accounts.google.com:anyone@finngen.fi with no bearer, and get fully authenticated results-api access - summary statistics, LD, sumstats ranges - under a forged identity, with no session attribution, no audience binding, no token lifetime and no cost cap.

FIX (do not do these blind - the from-less rule may be load-bearing for the GCP load balancer health checks, which is probably why it is there):
(a) make the X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email path conditional on a trusted-proxy marker that only auth-gateway can set, rather than on the header alone.
(b) tighten allow-ingress-results-api so the from-less rule is scoped, after confirming what actually needs it (LB health checks, bff, monitor).

Same pattern is worth checking on bff (allow-ingress-bff at policies.yaml:35-42 has the identical from-less shape on port 5000).
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: investigate first, then fix both layers. Nothing gets changed blind.

STEP 1 (read-only, no production change): determine what actually reaches results-api:4000 today and therefore what the from-less ingress rule in k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml is carrying. Candidates: GCP load-balancer health checks (check k8s/ingress/backend-configs.yaml for the health-check path and whether the LB targets results-api directly or only via auth-gateway), bff, monitor, chat-backend, mcp-server. The monitor CronJob's own policy already allows it to reach results-api:4000, which is evidence the from-less rule may not be needed for that. Report findings BEFORE editing anything.

STEP 2: (a) make the X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email path in genetics-results-api/app/core/auth.py get_verified_user conditional on a trusted-proxy marker only auth-gateway can set - auth-gateway already blanks the header at auth-gateway.yaml:120 and sets it from the verified oauth2-proxy email at 145/163/178/210, so the marker rides the same path; (b) scope the from-less rule to exactly what step 1 found.

Both are production changes. Do step 1 and present the findings; do not apply step 2 without explicit approval.

Blocks genetics-results-suite-4h6.8.

title: Node pool pinning was never applied to any live profile - autoscaler eviction fix is not in effect
description:
Found while reviewing the sandbox security design (genetics-results-suite-4h6.5) on 2026-08-07.

Commit 6db94e8 'fix: stop autoscaler evicting chat-backend mid-stream' pinned min_node_count == max_node_count == 2 to stop the autoscaler adding a node for a rollout and then scaling it down ~15 min later, evicting chat-backend mid-SSE. Its own message says: 'terraform/terraform.tfvars is gitignored, so the pinning is captured in terraform.tfvars.example; the live tfvars has been updated separately and still needs a terraform apply.'

That never happened. Verified 2026-08-07:
- terraform/terraform.tfvars (active): min_node_count = 1, max_node_count = 3
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.finngen: min = 1, max = 3
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.daly: min = 1, max = 2
- terraform/terraform.tfvars.example (the ONLY one tracked in git): min = 2, max = 2
- kubectl get nodes: exactly ONE e2-standard-4 node running

So the pinning exists only in the tracked example and in docs/project-spec.md. No live profile has it, and terraform apply was never run. The eviction bug the commit describes is still live: a full deploy.sh surges to 3951m CPU / 13.6 GiB against one node's 3920m / 12.97 GiB allocatable, so the autoscaler still adds a node and still scales it back down.

The graceful-shutdown half of that commit (terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300, preStop sleep 10, uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280) IS live - it is in the committed manifest. So the symptom is partly mitigated but the cause is not.

Also: docs/project-spec.md 'Node pool sizing' (~line 274-310) documents the 2/2 pinning as current fact. It is wrong, and the CLAUDE.md rule says a doc is stale the moment it enumerates something the code no longer matches.

Decide and then do ONE of:
(a) apply the pinning to the live tfvars profiles and terraform apply, or
(b) keep autoscaling and update docs/project-spec.md to describe reality, accepting the eviction risk or mitigating it another way (PodDisruptionBudget, which the namespace still lacks entirely).

Blocks genetics-results-suite-4h6.10 (node pool budget for the sandbox): the gVisor-on-a-separate-pool cost argument in docs/code-execution-security.md assumes the 2/2 pinning, and that premise is currently false.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: keep autoscaling (min 1 / max 3), fix the docs to describe reality, and add a PodDisruptionBudget. Do NOT apply the min==max==2 pinning.

Rationale for the choice: the namespace has NO PodDisruptionBudget at all today and every deployment is replicas:1, so node auto-upgrade and repair interrupt chat regardless of whether the pool is pinned. A PDB addresses a failure mode pinning does not, at no standing cost. The graceful-shutdown half of commit 6db94e8 (terminationGracePeriodSeconds 300, preStop sleep 10, uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 280) IS live and already cushions the eviction symptom.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD IS NOW:
1. Rewrite docs/project-spec.md 'Node pool sizing' (~274-310) to describe the real 1-3 autoscaling. It currently documents a 2/2 pinning as current fact, which is false in every live profile. Keep the surge-budget arithmetic (3951m vs 3920m, 13.60 vs 12.97 GiB) - that part is accurate and still explains why a rollout adds a node.
2. Add k8s/poddisruptionbudget.yaml covering at minimum chat-backend, and decide whether results-api/db-api/mcp-server need one. With replicas:1, minAvailable:1 blocks voluntary eviction entirely - confirm that is what is wanted versus maxUnavailable:0, and note it will make node drains require manual intervention.
3. Update terraform.tfvars.example so the tracked file stops claiming 2/2.

Do NOT run terraform apply for this bead.

title: Run the paired benchmark and decide the rollout on the numbers
description:
Run replay_benchmark.py with the code arm against the current all-tools arm.

Report DISTRIBUTIONS. A code-execution arm scores ~1 tool call by construction, so tool-call count alone is a dishonest win condition. The gate is the combination:
- iterations per turn (baseline median 2, p90 6, p95 8, max 25)
- total input+output tokens and USD (baseline mean 2.01 USD/turn; 13.5% of turns over 5 iterations consume 35% of spend)
- wall-clock to first token and to done (watch for regression on the 36% of turns that are single-iteration today - a sandbox adds fixed cost there)
- script failure rate and retry-loop count
- LLM-judge quality via analyze_conversations --force, which must not regress

Expected shape of the win, from the 2026-08-07 measurement: cost and tail latency, NOT a dramatic median tool-call drop. Median context grows 39k -> 117k tokens between iteration 1 and 7+ while the uncached share rises 11% -> 52%; keeping intermediate data out of context is the mechanism being tested.

Kill criterion: if the code arm does not beat the baseline on cost AND does not regress quality, keep it behind the profile rather than defaulting it on.

title: Add the code TOOL_PROFILE and exclude code execution from /mcp
description:
Add a 'code' entry to TOOL_PROFILES (definitions.py:1558) holding the five-tool surface: run_analysis, list_capabilities, read_artifact, search_entities, search_literature. Ship it dark, A/B it via the existing per-request tool_profile (chat_api.py:277, persisted in chat_messages.tool_profile, defaulted per user via chat_tool_profile), then flip the server-side default. Rollback is one constant.

Separately and non-negotiably: run_analysis and read_artifact must be added to _mcp_disabled (mcp_server.py:84-94) so the standalone MCP server never registers them. The user requires that people cannot execute code via MCP calls. Add a test asserting these names are absent from the /mcp tool list. This is the tool-registration layer; the NetworkPolicy task is the second layer.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/definitions.py, mcp_server.py, tests/test_mcp_server.py.

title: Implement run_analysis: submit code, stream stdout, enforce caps
description:
The single tool that replaces the data-access grid. Submits model-authored Python to the sandbox, streams stdout back, and enforces wall-clock timeout, output size cap and memory limit per the security doc.

Failure handling matters as much as the happy path: the benchmark counts script failures and retries because a failing script costs a full model roundtrip, and the realistic risk is a bimodal distribution (most turns at 1-2 roundtrips, a tail at 8+ from debugging loops). Return errors as structured, actionable messages (traceback plus the relevant stub) so the model repairs in one attempt rather than three.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/definitions.py, tools/executor.py, sandbox client (new).

title: Extract ToolExecutor data methods into an importable genetics SDK
description:
Turn the existing per-tool executor methods into a stable Python package the sandbox imports: genetics.credible_sets(gene=..), genetics.coloc(..), genetics.sumstats(..), genetics.ld(..), genetics.mpra(..), genetics.sql(..) etc. This is a refactor, not a rewrite - the HTTP/tabix/BigQuery logic in executor.py (4,679 lines) is kept, only the entry points change.

One function per data product, with the by_gene/by_variant/by_region/by_phenotype distinction becoming ARGUMENTS rather than separate names. That grid is what produced 42 near-duplicate tools in the first place.

Note five methods already issue server-written SQL against BigQuery (executor.py:878, 1021, 1080, 1159, 1197) - use them as the pattern, and fix their f-string SQL interpolation while moving them.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ (new package), tools/executor.py.
close_reason:
genetics SDK landed. genetics-mcp-server worktree commit 5f1ba16. Suite 1024 -> 1165 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. Two reviewers (behaviour-preservation + adversarial security), one fix round.

17 SDK functions replace 42 entry points, THIN over the existing executor - no HTTP/tabix/BigQuery logic moved, because the 42 MCP tools stay the production surface until .16.

TICKET FRAMING CORRECTED: the grid does not collapse completely. mpra_pip_concordance is a JOIN of credible_sets_v and mpra_v with a different row shape, so it stays its own function. normalize_gene_symbols was initially omitted on the grounds its 'unresolved' list cannot be a DataFrame - review disagreed (one row per input with a null symbol is the tidy form) and it is now included, along with lookup_phenotype_names and get_dataset_display_names, without which a script cannot resolve the trait CODES that credible_sets/summary_stats/gene_burden return.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - none of these failed a test:
- The five BigQuery paths returned TRANSPOSED, STRINGIFIED frames. db-api returns rows positionally with names in a separate key; the SDK used pl.from_dicts. It did not raise - it fabricated column_0/column_1 names and coerced everything to str. Green only because two test mocks disagreed about the same upstream.
- 61 caller-controlled URL path segments were unencoded, and httpx normalises dot segments: mpra(variant='../../admin/users') reached an arbitrary results-api endpoint on the same host WITH THE INTERNAL BEARER ATTACHED. Strictly wider than the SQL hole the task was written to close.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not by reading: percent-encoding does NOT break colon-separated identifiers (real uvicorn+FastAPI server; uvicorn unquotes scope['path'] before Starlette routes; no route uses a path converter; auth-gateway's proxy_pass has no URI part so nginx forwards verbatim). '.' and '..' now work where they used to 404. _gene_window_cte generates byte-identical SQL for all five methods. The MCP payload is byte-identical without with_metadata. The import-isolation test uses a real subprocess.

REFRAMING WORTH KEEPING: sql_safety guards the MCP surface, NOT the SDK. A script can call sql() with arbitrary SQL, so what actually stands between it and BigQuery is db-api's SELECT-only check, its table allow-list and MAX_BYTES_BILLED. The hardening is still worth having where values are model-chosen and there is no escape hatch.

CONSEQUENCE FOR .9/.14: configure() is concrete evidence for what code-execution-security.md asserts - if the SDK runs inside the sandbox, INTERNAL_API_SECRET must not be there at all, since a script that can import can read os.environ. The scoped token is load-bearing, not optional hardening.

title: Scoped short-lived credential for sandbox to db-api
description:
The sandbox must never hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. That secret authenticates the service, not the request, and a script that can read it can reach db-api directly and forever.

Design and implement a per-request, short-lived, audience-scoped token minted by chat-backend and injected into the sandbox execution environment for the lifetime of one script. db-api validates it alongside the existing shared secret. Include an expiry short enough that a leaked token is worthless (minutes), and make the token carry the session id so db-api logs attribute queries to a conversation.

Note the fail-open behaviour in db-api today (docs/project-spec.md: unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET disables auth with a startup warning) - the new path must NOT inherit fail-open.

Files: genetics-results-db/api/main.py, genetics-mcp-server sandbox client, k8s manifests.

title: NetworkPolicy: sandbox egress allow-list, and mcp-server must not reach it
description:
Two directions, both required.

Egress FROM sandbox: db-api (8080) and results-api (4000) only. Deny all other egress including DNS-to-internet, so a script cannot exfiltrate query results or fetch code. Deny access to keycloak, keycloak-postgres, chat-backend and rag-service.

Ingress TO sandbox: chat-backend ONLY. mcp-server must be denied at the network layer, not just by omitting the tool - this is the user's explicit requirement that code execution not be reachable via MCP, and the suite spec already warns (docs/project-spec.md:237) that mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api policy, so a tool-registration omission alone is not a boundary.

Add a test that asserts the mcp-server pod cannot open a connection to the sandbox Service.

Files: k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (new), docs/project-spec.md (Security section).

title: Build the paired A/B replay benchmark harness
description:
New scripts/replay_benchmark.py. POSTs recorded turn sequences to /chat/v1/chat with secret=true (chat_api.py:295, so nothing is persisted) under two tool_profile arms in a PAIRED design - both arms in one execution so model drift cannot confound the comparison.

Report DISTRIBUTIONS, not just medians: production is heavily tail-weighted (median 2 iterations but p95 8, max 25). Metrics per arm: iterations/turn, tool calls/turn, wall-clock to first token and to done, input/output/cache tokens, USD. Plus code-execution-specific counters: script failure rate (non-zero exit, timeout, exception) and retry-loop count, since a failing script costs a full roundtrip.

Baseline to beat, measured 2026-08-07 over 916 turns since 2026-05-01: iterations median 2 / p90 6 / p95 8; tool calls per turn median 4 / p90 12; mean 2.01 USD per turn; 13.5% of turns >5 iterations consuming 35% of spend; median context 39k tokens at iteration 1 growing to 117k at iteration 7+ with uncached share rising 11% -> 52%.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/scripts/replay_benchmark.py (new).
notes:
HANDOFF from .1 (2026-08-07): .4's plan is to POST with secret=true 'so nothing is persisted' (chat_api.py:295). With .1 landed, secret=true ALSO means no chat_turn_metrics row is written — .1 deliberately skips metrics entirely for secret chat because secret chat is a privacy promise to the user. So the replay harness CANNOT read its numbers out of chat_turn_metrics when running secret.

Two options, pick one and record it: (a) read iterations/tokens/cost off the SSE stream itself — llm_service.py already yields a 'usage' StreamChunk per iteration carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent; or (b) run non-secret against a throwaway copy of chat_history.db and read chat_turn_metrics.

(a) is probably better: it needs no DB at all and works against any deployment.

ENVIRONMENT TRAP: in a fresh genetics-mcp-server worktree, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the pyenv shim rather than the worktree venv and imported genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT, silently testing unmodified source. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' first, then assert the module resolves inside the worktree before trusting any test result.
close_reason:
Paired A/B replay harness built. genetics-mcp-server worktree fbf121e. Suite 1165 -> 1194 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. One reviewer, one fix round.

BUILD ONLY - running it against a deployment is task .23, separately gated. Default base URL is localhost, --dry-run issues zero requests, secret=true is a hard-coded literal with no flag or env override.

THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS:
1. The usage chunk's input_tokens is the WHOLE CONTEXT (input_tok + cache_read + cache_create), not billed input. Cached tokens are derived by subtracting total_input_tokens.
2. COST CANNOT BE COMPUTED EXACTLY FROM THE STREAM. Cache reads and creations are folded into one number and never separated, yet they differ by exactly 12.5x in price. The harness reports an INTERVAL (all-cached-as-reads to all-cached-as-creations) rather than fabricating a figure; since every per-token price lies between those, the true cost is provably inside it. This weakens the metric .23 gates on - production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% to 52% across a turn, so the interval will not be narrow. Fix filed as genetics-results-suite-n3p: emit cache_read/cache_create on the usage chunk. Both are already computed and already logged one line away.
3. An unpriceable --model was silently priced as Sonnet by cost.py's fallback. Now warns and returns null.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - either would have INVERTED the result:
- Replayed history dropped tool_results. Production pushes them back as a user turn (LLMChat.tsx ~595-599); without them _sanitize_tool_blocks strips every tool_use block from the replayed assistant turn as orphaned, so from turn 2 the model saw an answer from thin air. Tool results are the BULK of the context growth this epic exists to measure (39k -> 117k, uncached 11% -> 52%), and the bias was ASYMMETRIC - the arm making more tool calls lost more context, compressing the measured gap toward zero. A code-execution arm would have looked no better than the status quo.
- The paired design was never used in the ANALYSIS. Distributions were built per arm independently over ok turns, so an arm failing on the hard, late, expensive turns kept only its cheap early ones and its medians dropped BECAUSE it failed. Recording failures is not excluding them from the comparison. Matched subset (ok in both arms) is now the headline; marginals survive explicitly labelled not-comparable.

ALSO FIXED: a wedged stream could keepalive past the per-turn timeout forever (httpx read timeout is per-read and sse-starlette comments reset it, so the TimeoutError handler was dead code); a whole-case exception collapsed N turns into 2 records; a turn with no usage chunk contributed a fake tool_calls=0, which EVERY turn would do against a deployment defaulting to OpenAI (--provider added); MIN_N_FOR_PERCENTILE[90] was 11 not 10 through float error.

VERIFIED CORRECT BY REVIEW: tool calls counted from real tool_use blocks never the prose markers (.2's imitation finding); the cost interval is a true bound computed the right way round; semaphore scope makes arms of one case non-overlapping; arm alternation recorded per case; per-turn failure aborts only that case+arm.

DESIGNED-IN GUARDS: percentiles flagged unreliable when n(1-p) < 1 so a p90 from 9 cases is not presented as stable; script_runs/script_failures/retry_loops look for a chunk that does not exist yet and stay None with an explicit NOT MEASURED reason, so the eventual code-execution arm cannot win trivially on a silent zero.

title: ChatRequest.system_prompt lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt
description:
Flagged during planning of the Instructions epic (genetics-results-suite-s5y) and deliberately left out of its scope. Now in scope on its own.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:215 declares ChatRequest.system_prompt, used verbatim at ~line 458:
    system_prompt = request.system_prompt or default_system_prompt(settings.app_name)
There is no allow-list, no admin gate, no length bound. Any authenticated caller can replace the ENTIRE system prompt for their turn - discarding every grounding, citation, truncation and out-of-scope rule the default prompt establishes.

This is a strictly larger hole than the feature built next to it. The Instructions epic went to some length to make user-authored text safe: the body is resolved server-side by id so it never travels on the request, it is capped, it is wrapped in an envelope with a trailing guardrail, and it is scoped to presentation only. All of that is bypassed by a field sitting two lines away that accepts arbitrary prompt text with no constraints at all.

SCOPING ALREADY DONE - nothing in the suite sends it:
- genetics-results-browser: zero references in src/ or bff/
- the only senders anywhere are tests (tests/test_chat_api.py:356 test_chat_custom_system_prompt, and the stream-truncation harness which passes system_prompt=None)
- llm_service.stream_chat(system_prompt=...) is a separate INTERNAL parameter that chat_api populates with the assembled default+verbosity prompt. That stays; only the request-level override is the hole.

Preferred fix: remove the field from ChatRequest entirely. Pydantic ignores unknown fields by default, so a caller still sending it is silently ignored rather than 422'd - a graceful removal with no client breakage.

Before removing, confirm there is no external consumer: the chat API is also reachable with a bearer API token (see the Authorization: Bearer path that bypasses the BFF), so check whether any script, notebook or sibling repo drives it directly. If a legitimate need exists, the fallback is an admin gate plus a length bound rather than leaving it open.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit f8302b9. Suite 935 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds.

Removed rather than gated, after confirming across all six repos that nothing sends it - not the browser, not the BFF, not any script; only a test. Pydantic ignores unknown keys, so a caller still sending it is ignored rather than 422'd. A side benefit: block 0 of the two-block cached system prompt is now unconditionally identical across users, which its cache design already assumed.

THE SAME CAPABILITY EXISTED IN A SECOND FORM, found independently by both reviewers and fixed here too: the Anthropic path filtered client-sent system-role messages but the OpenAI path did not, and provider is client-selectable with OPENAI_API_KEY wired into the pod, so a system-role message landed AFTER the server prompt where recency favours it. Rather than filter per provider, ChatMessage.role is now Literal['user','assistant'] - the authority boundary is the request model. Both provider filters stay as defence in depth because stream_chat is reachable with raw dicts.

422 rather than a silent drop: the history endpoint already rejects those roles, so no caller has reason to send one, and quietly discarding an injection attempt hides it from the caller and the logs.

Verified no real flow breaks: the browser builds message history only from stored rows plus hardcoded user literals; chat_history.py:414 rejects non-user/assistant at persistence and add_message has exactly one caller, so no system-role row can exist to be replayed; fork copies roles from rows that already passed that check.

Corrected a false claim I had put in the bead and the docs: the chat API is NOT reachable with a per-user API token. auth_required accepts the IAP/oauth2-proxy header or a Bearer INTERNAL_API_SECRET resolving to identity 'mcp-tool'; per-user tokens are validated only by the internal-only /tokens/validate that the /mcp path consumes. The security argument is unaffected - any IAP-authenticated user could already do it.

Follow-ups filed: the tool-descriptions authz gap, and the assistant-role length bound.

title: Phase 0: decide ChromBPNet row-scale thresholding policy
description: Count ChromBPNet variant-score rows (132 contexts x variants, potentially billions). Decide thresholding (significant/non-zero only, or top-N per context) before sizing tabix/BQ. Biggest scale risk. Gates the Marderstein munge task.
design:
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT thresholding policy (empirical cutoff + row counts to be CONFIRMED once data is downloaded — blocked on .1). Keep this task OPEN.
Problem: ChromBPNet = 132 contexts x all variants (~3 billion predictions in the paper). Do NOT store the full cross-product.
Default:
- ChromBPNet -> variant_effect (model=chrombpnet), LONG. Emit a row only for (variant, context) pairs that pass a significance/effect threshold, NOT all 132 contexts per variant. Prefer the per-context significance calls provided by the Synapse release if present; else keep per-context empirical mlog10p >= 3 (p <= 1e-3) OR abs(chrombpnet_logfc) in the top 1 percent per context. Always set is_significant and mlog10p so the cutoff is transparent and re-filterable.
- Retain a variant if significant in ANY context (so by_variant lookups return it); emit its passing contexts, plus optionally its single top context.
- FLARE -> variant_effect (model=flare): keep the FULL released FLARE prioritized-variant set (already curated and far smaller); pan-context rows with cell_type/tissue NULL.
Rationale: bounds storage to variants with a real predicted effect somewhere (millions, not billions) — exactly what the query needs. Empirical step (after .1): count rows at this cutoff, confirm the significance fields the release actually provides, adjust cutoff to a sane table size.

title: usage SSE chunk folds cache reads and creations together, so cost cannot be computed exactly
description:
Found building the replay harness (genetics-results-suite-4h6.4) on 2026-08-07. Small change, disproportionate value.

llm_service.py emits a per-iteration 'usage' StreamChunk carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent.

TWO PROBLEMS for anything measuring cost off the stream:

1. The chunk's input_tokens is NOT the billed input. llm_service.py ~786 sets it to input_tok + cache_read + cache_create - i.e. the whole context - while total_input_tokens accumulates only raw input_tok. Anyone reading input_tokens as billed input overstates it, badly, on a cache-heavy turn.

2. Cache READS and cache CREATIONS are folded into that single number and never separated. They differ by more than 12x in price (Opus: ~0.50 vs ~6.25 per M tokens). So an exact USD figure cannot be derived from the stream at all.

The replay harness works around (2) by reporting an INTERVAL - cost_usd_min pricing all cached tokens as reads, cost_usd_max pricing them all as creations - rather than fabricating a single number. That is honest but it weakens the primary metric that genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 gates the whole code-execution rollout on. Production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% -> 52% across a turn's iterations, so the interval will not be narrow.

FIX: add cache_read and cache_create to the usage StreamChunk payload in llm_service.py. Both values are already computed and logged one line above (the 'API call iteration=' log line carries cache_read= and cache_create=), so this is exposing what already exists, not new instrumentation. Then the harness can compute exact cost and drop the interval.

Note chat_turn_metrics (task .1) DOES store cache_read_tokens and cache_create_tokens separately - but the benchmark runs with secret=true, which writes no row, which is why it reads the stream instead. This is the gap between those two paths.

title: Worktree venv trap: uv run resolves to the pyenv shim and tests the main checkout
description:
Discovered 2026-08-07 while implementing genetics-results-suite-4h6.1.

In a freshly created git worktree of genetics-mcp-server, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the PYENV SHIM (/home/jkarjala/.pyenv/shims/pytest) rather than the worktree's own venv — pytest was never installed in the worktree .venv. That global interpreter imports genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT at /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/src.

Consequence: a test run in the worktree silently exercises MAIN CHECKOUT source against WORKTREE tests. Edits made in the worktree are invisible, and the run reports green. The baseline established this way (977 passed) happened to be numerically correct only because both trees were at the same clean commit b2a1df4 — had the main checkout been dirty, every result would have been meaningless.

FIX for any agent working in a genetics-mcp-server worktree:
1. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' in the worktree (installs the declared dev extra into the existing venv; does not create a new one).
2. ASSERT resolution before trusting any result:
     uv run python -c "import genetics_mcp_server, sys; print(genetics_mcp_server.__file__); print(sys.executable)"
   Both paths must be under the worktree.

Corrected baseline after the fix: 977 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed (~150s), verified under two pytest-randomly seeds. pytest-randomly 4.1.0 IS installed and active, so the suite is genuinely shuffled and order dependence is tested.

Worth considering whether to make this fail loudly rather than relying on every agent remembering — e.g. a conftest.py assertion that the imported package path is under the rootdir.

title: Feature: code-execution agent — genetics SDK in a hardened sandbox, minimal tool surface
description:
Reduce the chat/MCP agent's tool surface (currently 63 tools, 42 of them API-bound) by making BigQuery the primary data path, keeping genetics-results-api as a specialist backend for what BQ cannot serve (summary statistics, LD, fuzzy search index, streaming downloads) and for the browser/BFF.

Motivation:
1. Tool-count bloat: 63 tools is far above the 5-15 practical ceiling where tool-selection accuracy degrades; the 42 API tools dominate per-turn schema overhead.
2. BigQuery is strictly more capable than the tabix API for the verticals it already holds, because it can JOIN (cis/trans, caQTL peak->gene, gene groups).
3. Reduce tool calls per conversation - table/schema design and front-loaded example SQL directly drive round-trip count.
4. Fill BQ data gaps and revisit partitioning/clustering for latency.

Hard constraints discovered during examination:
- Summary statistics cannot move to BQ (~10^11 rows, source buckets not owned by the suite).
- LD is panel-computed, not tabular.
- Fuzzy phenotype/gene search is an in-memory ranked index; BQ cannot replace it.
- The API's largest consumer is the browser via BFF, independent of chat - API retirement is NOT in scope, only tool retirement.

Gate: a benchmark built from real production conversations (chat_history.db) must be in place BEFORE migration, measuring tool calls/turn, latency, token cost and answer quality.
notes:

title: PUT tool-descriptions is auth_required, not admin_required
description:
Found by the blind validator while fixing genetics-results-suite-uog. PRE-EXISTING and currently DORMANT, but it is a latent global prompt-injection channel.

genetics-mcp-server routers/llm_config.py:557-565 - PUT /chat/v1/llm-config/tool-descriptions/{tool_name} is gated by auth_required, not admin_required. Any authenticated user can overwrite a GLOBAL tool description with unbounded free text, persisted and versioned in tool_description_history.

Why it still matters: the moment anything wires those rows in, one user's edit reaches every user's turn. Tool descriptions are the instructions the model uses to decide WHEN to call a tool, so a hostile or careless edit is more consequential than an instruction set, which is per-user and presentation-scoped.

Fix: change the dependency to admin_required, matching the other global-configuration endpoints. Check the DELETE and any sibling write on the same resource. Note this is an authz change on a route that currently has no legitimate non-admin user, so it should break nothing - confirm no client calls it (the browser's llmConfigApi.ts only calls the comments endpoints).

Also from the same review, weaker and separate: request.model is unvalidated against any allowlist - a cost and scope question rather than prompt text.

All four legacy /llm-config/tool-descriptions* endpoints now Depends(admin_required), not just the PUT: the two GETs return changed_by (an admin email), and admin-to-write/world-to-read invites the write gate being read as accidental. No DELETE exists on the resource. Confirmed no caller outside tests across all six repos. Consequence worth knowing: admin_required 404s when ENABLE_ADMIN_PAGE=false; prod sets it true in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml. The suite runs REQUIRE_AUTH=false where admin_required waves everyone through, so pre-existing tests would have passed unchanged and proved nothing - added TestToolDescriptionAuthGuards which moves REQUIRE_AUTH/ADMIN_USERS itself, plus an admin_client fixture enabling ENABLE_ADMIN_PAGE for the existing cases. title: test suite has order-dependent failures under pytest-randomly
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-2cl/-qdf. PRE-EXISTING and reproducible on pristine HEAD — confirmed NOT caused by that work (a reviewer built a tree differing only by a test-fixture move and got byte-identical failure sets).

genetics-mcp-server: with pytest-randomly active, TestAdminAuthGuards::test_dev_mode_allows_any_user (expects 200, gets 404) and ::test_non_admin_denied_when_auth_required (expects 403, gets 404) fail under some seeds. Measured: seeds 12345 and 20260804 FAIL; seeds 1, 42, 999, 7 PASS. Roughly a 1-in-3 hit rate. With -p no:randomly the suite is green.

The tests pass when test_admin_router.py runs alone under the failing seed, so the leak comes from OTHER modules running first, and no single module reproduces it in isolation — it needs a combination.

Diagnosed causes (not fixed):
- config/settings.py get_settings() is @lru_cache'd; tests that call it without clearing the cache leave a stale Settings instance behind, and admin_required then sees enable_admin_page=False and 404s.
- auth/dependencies.py:14 evaluates _require_auth = os.environ.get('REQUIRE_AUTH', ...) at IMPORT time, so patching os.environ later does not update it.

Fix likely means an autouse fixture clearing get_settings.cache_clear() between tests, and reading REQUIRE_AUTH through settings rather than at import time.

This matters beyond flakiness: every 'full suite green' claim in this epic's task history was measured on whatever seed happened to run.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit adb57ef. Suite 810 passed / 74 deselected on -p no:randomly and on seeds 12345, 20260804, 1, 987654321 — the first two being the known-bad ones.

THE TICKET'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG and was corrected during implementation. It blamed a stale @lru_cache on get_settings(); the two failing tests already call cache_clear() themselves. The real cause: test_temperature.py called importlib.reload on the settings module, rebinding config.settings.get_settings to a new function object with its own empty cache while config/__init__.py kept re-exporting the old one. admin_required reads the package handle, the tests cleared the submodule handle. A reviewer proved causality by re-injecting the reload into the fixed tree and reproducing the exact failure set.

The reload was never needed (every Settings field reads os.environ in a default_factory) and was latently harmful (the module calls load_dotenv() at import, so a reload resurrects an env var a test just removed).

SEPARATE FINDING, now fixed: pytest-randomly was neither installed nor declared, so -p no:randomly was a silent no-op and every seed sweep in this epic ran against ad-hoc installs. Declared and pinned exactly (the seed-to-order mapping moves between versions), with shuffling left on by default — an undeclared plugin is how this went unnoticed.

Follow-up filed for the REQUIRE_AUTH two-sources-of-truth test trap.

title: llm_config_db: write accessors leave the transaction open on failure
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.4. In genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py, none of these write accessors roll back on failure: save_tool_description, add_user_comment, delete_user_comment, save_user_setting, delete_user_setting, create_api_token, revoke_api_token, validate_api_token.

Each is a single DML, so SQLite has already backed out that statement's own changes and no partial data is pending. But the transaction stays OPEN and holds the write lock against every other writer of llm_config.db until that thread happens to commit something else. Connections are thread-local and cached for the process lifetime, so a long-lived server thread can hold the lock indefinitely.

The instruction-set accessors added in s5y.4 have rollback guards and a _discard_stale_transaction helper that incidentally cleans this up whenever one of them next runs on the same thread — nothing else does.

Fix: mirror the try/except BaseException -> rollback; raise pattern from create_instruction_set, and move conn.commit() inside the try.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 56f2341. Suite 770 passed / 74 deselected, stable over 6 repeat runs; 20 of 21 new tests verified to fail against the unfixed source.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION on the auth path, verified security-neutral by two independent reviewers: validate_api_token swallows a failure of its trailing bookkeeping UPDATE (last_used_at + rolling expiry) and returns the user anyway, rather than raising. Revocation (is_active=1 in the SELECT's WHERE) and expiry are both decided BEFORE the try, from committed state, so no invalid/expired/revoked token can authenticate. The deadline is frozen rather than pushed on failure, so a persistently failing write ages a token out rather than keeping it alive. Old behaviour was strictly worse: the raise became a 500, mcp-server read that as 401, and the poisoned connection failed every subsequent validation on the same thread — one transient SQLITE_BUSY became a lasting 401 outage for all API-token users until pod restart.

Scope note: read accessors also got _discard_stale_transaction (12 methods the ticket did not name). Kept as defence-in-depth and documented as such, not as a live bug fix.

Follow-up filed: genetics-results-suite-4um (chat_history_db.py has the identical bug class).

title: Fix same-second tiebreak in user-settings reads
description: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py get_user_setting/get_user_settings (~lines 452-506). They join on MAX(changed_at), but SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP has 1-second resolution, so two saves to the same key in the same second both match and an arbitrary winner is kept. Add ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC (id is a true AUTOINCREMENT sequence). Needed because the selected-set pointer will live in this store.

Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 416e961. Suite 785 passed / 74 deselected across 5 runs including 2 random orderings. Blind validation killed all 8 mutants (HEAD revert of each of the 5 queries, MAX->MIN on both grouped forms, and dropping the user_id scope); 11 of 12 new tests fail against HEAD, the survivor being the one that pins preserved NULL behaviour.

The bug was user-visible, not latent: the index is scanned rowid-ascending within a tie, so get_user_setting returned the OLDEST tied write every time. Two clicks inside one second kept the first.

TWO ROUNDS OF REGRESSION CAUGHT IN REVIEW: (1) the first rewrite lost the index on both plural accessors — measured 26ms->1124ms at 60k tool rows and 5.5->214ms at 10k settings rows/user. Replaced with a grouped MAX(id) form that restores the plan and matches or beats HEAD. (2) A comment asserted a query plan that only occurs after ANALYZE; neither repo ever runs ANALYZE, so it was wrong in the deployed state. Two reviewers contradicted each other on it and the disagreement was resolved empirically across 44 database states.

SCOPE BEYOND THE TICKET, needs the user's awareness: the ticket named only get_user_setting/get_user_settings. Three tool-description accessors carried the identical defect and were also fixed — fixing only the singular one would have made it disagree with the history listing an admin reads as current, and a tie there could drop the NEWEST versions from a limited listing. Deliberately NOT touched: get_user_comments/list_all_user_comments (tie permutes a display list, no current value derived) — filed as genetics-results-suite-qdf instead.

title: Feature: user-authored Instructions for chat
description:
Users can create and store multiple named sets of additional instructions (like Claude Desktop 'profiles', e.g. 'I'm a statistician') and select one per chat use case. The selected profile's text is appended to the LLM system prompt on each chat request.

UI lands beside the existing brief/detailed Answer selector in the chat options row (genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx). Storage is per-user in the DB (genetics-mcp-server SQLite llm_config_db, which already has user_settings_history and an orphaned user_instructions_history table). Backend prompt assembly mirrors the verbosity_prompt() pattern in config/defaults.py + chat_api.py.

Spans repos: genetics-mcp-server (API + DB + prompt), genetics-results-browser (UI + types), genetics-results-suite (docs of record).

Naming to be decided as part of planning.
design:
Alternative 2 selected: first-class entity, server-resolved by id, split cached system block.

Name: UI label 'Instructions', code noun instruction_set. Rejected 'profile' (already means tool_profile in the same options row, the daly/finngen deploy config_profile, and results-api app/config/profiles/), 'persona' (the suite spec uses it for the APP_NAME assistant persona, and the text describes the user not the assistant) and 'context' (the same row renders a 'Conversation context' usage bar).

Key decisions:
- The chat request carries an id only; the server loads the body scoped to the authenticated user, so prompt text is never client-supplied and an answer is always attributable to a stored set.
- System prompt splits into two cached blocks: shared default+verbosity (one global cache entry per verbosity value) and the per-user envelope on the spare 4th breakpoint. ~$0.0025 per incremental write vs ~$0.043 for full-block refragmentation vs ~$0.05 per 25-iteration turn uncached.
- Selection: global-per-user default in user_settings_history, overridden per request, recorded per message on chat_messages. Per-session storage rejected: it needs a session-mutation endpoint and makes 'which wins' unanswerable when the selector moves mid-conversation.
- Archive rather than delete, so historical chat_messages rows stay resolvable.
- Unknown id is ignored, never 422 — same rule as verbosity.
- Folded in from the other alternatives: seeded clonable example sets in the dialog (from Alt 3), and the ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC settings fix (from Alt 1).

Out of scope, documented rather than built: subagents (their reports are intermediate artifacts the main agent rewrites) and the MCP server path (no server-side system prompt, _validate_user_token discards identity, no llm_config.db volume mounted).

Not part of this epic, but decide separately: ChatRequest.system_prompt (chat_api.py:209) lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate — a strictly larger hole than the feature going in beside it.
close_reason:
All 21 subtasks closed. Feature complete and documented across genetics-mcp-server, genetics-results-browser and this repo's spec of record.

Shipped: users author named instruction sets, pick one per chat, and the selected set's text is appended to the system prompt in its own cached block. Named 'Instructions' rather than 'profiles' because tool_profile already sits in the same options row and the deploy config_profile and results-api app/config/profiles/ take the word twice more.

Architecture as chosen (Alternative 2): a first-class entity, resolved server-side by id so prompt text never travels on the request, with the system prompt split into a shared cached block and a per-user one. That keeps one cache entry per verbosity value instead of fragmenting per user, and consumes the fourth and last Anthropic breakpoint.

Blocking bugs caught in review that a green test suite did not: a read-time clamp that destroyed 5000 chars of a 9000-char legacy set on an edit round-trip; a per-user cap four concurrent requests walked straight through; BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside a try permanently poisoning a thread's cached connection; a fixed markdown fence a body could close early to inject a fake system section; an unvalidated LIMIT that returned entire histories on ?limit=-1 and 500'd past 64 bits; and a selector that silently reset on every session switch so messages went without the user's instructions.

Also fixed along the way, all pre-existing: rollback guards across both SQLite modules, WAL on llm_config.db, a same-second tiebreak that returned the OLDEST write, malformed-timestamp crashes, admin feedback pagination that could duplicate or skip an item, REQUIRE_AUTH read from two sources, and an importlib.reload that split the settings cache and made the suite's own green signal unreliable.

Deliberately not built, documented instead: instructions do not apply to subagents or to the MCP server path. Filed rather than fixed: genetics-results-suite-b3v (OpenAI branch drops instructions silently), -uvh (batched comment/doc accuracy), -eis (admin UI timestamp format), -avt (INTERNAL_API_SECRET), plus the still-open question of ChatRequest.system_prompt letting any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate.

title: [mcp-server] Serve MCP OAuth discovery (.well-known/oauth-protected-resource + WWW-Authenticate)
description:
Repo: ../genetics-mcp-server. File: src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py, in the ASGI auth_middleware (same place /healthz is special-cased).

Implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata so MCP clients (Claude connectors, ChatGPT, brainzzz) auto-discover the authorization server:
- Serve GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (and the path-suffixed /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp) returning JSON: { resource: OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL, authorization_servers: [OAUTH_ISSUER], scopes_supported: [...], bearer_methods_supported: ["header"] }. Serve it WITHOUT requiring a bearer token.
- On a 401 from the bearer middleware, add header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<resource>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" so clients know where to look.
Only enable these when OAUTH_ISSUER is configured. The authorization-server metadata itself (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) is served by Keycloak, not here.

title: Feature: Direct OAuth (Keycloak) auth for MCP server — GeneGenie / brainzzz
description:
Let external web applications (first: brainzzz) connect to the GeneGenie MCP server via a standard OAuth 2.1 flow, instead of a shared api-token. Add this as a FOURTH bearer-validation path alongside the existing three (MCP_API_KEY shared secret, Google Identity Token JWT, per-user API token) — nothing existing is removed.

WHY: IAP/Google ID-Tokens don't fit a third-party app acting on behalf of its own users (audience-bound, no consent/refresh, users not on our email allow-list). MCP's HTTP transport defines an OAuth 2.1 profile where the MCP server is an OAuth *resource server* and clients auto-discover the *authorization server*. The daly/GeneGenie deployment already runs Keycloak as a full OIDC AS (https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK on for daly), so Keycloak is the authorization server and a 'web application type' OAuth client registered there is exactly what's needed.

SCOPE: GeneGenie (daly profile) only for now. finngen/FinnGenie has Keycloak OFF (Google-direct) and is out of scope.

DESIGN CONTRACT (shared across subtasks):
- Authorization server = Keycloak realm 'genetics'; issuer https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics.
- MCP resource canonical URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator / RFC 9728 resource identifier) = https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp.
- Keycloak issues access tokens (JWT) with aud including that resource URL (via an audience mapper / dedicated client scope on the brainzzz client).
- MCP server validates: signature via Keycloak JWKS, iss match, aud includes resource URL, exp; THEN the existing email/domain allow-list (settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, already fed by the bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap).
- Discovery: MCP server serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) pointing at the Keycloak issuer, and returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer with resource_metadata=... on 401. The authorization-server metadata itself is served by Keycloak (already on auth.<domain>).

Code work is split between the sibling repo ../genetics-mcp-server (validation + discovery + settings) and this repo genetics-results-suite (deployment env + auth-gateway routing + docs). Plus Keycloak client config (ops).

title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

design:
Genome-build decision — platform standard = GRCh38/hg38 (GENCODE).
- marderstein (scATAC peaks + ChromBPNet + FLARE): hg38, native, no liftOver.
- li_brain_atac (Li 2023 Science): hg38, native.

- rosmap_brain (Xiong 2023): hg38, native.
RULE for every munge task: verify the source file build at download; if hg19, liftOver to hg38 and drop unmapped/multimapped before bgzip+tabix. Only Calderon is known-hg19 today.

title: No test proves URL path segments round-trip against a real ASGI server
description:
Coverage gap found during the re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07. The behaviour is CORRECT - this is about the suite not proving it.

Task .11 applied urllib.parse.quote(value, safe='') to 61 caller-controlled URL path segments in tools/executor.py. Since every identifier in this suite is colon-separated (variants are chr:pos:ref:alt, regions are chr:start-end), that encodes ':' as '%3A' on essentially every call.

The reviewer verified round-tripping empirically by standing up a real uvicorn + FastAPI server with routes mirroring the real signatures, and confirmed every realistic identifier survives byte-identically: variants with all four documented separators, regions, HLA-DRB1, MT-CO1, IGH@, Open_Targets_26.06, and values containing spaces, plus and percent. It also confirmed uvicorn unquotes scope['path'] before Starlette routing, that no route uses a path converter or custom regex, and that auth-gateway's proxy_pass has no URI part so nginx forwards the request URI verbatim.

But the SUITE only asserts containment: tests/test_bigquery_gene_tools.py:84 checks the URL still starts with the right prefix. Nothing asserts a positive round-trip for a colon-bearing identifier. So a future change to _seg(), to a route signature, or to the nginx proxy_pass could silently break every by-variant and by-region tool while the suite stays green.

FIX: add a test that runs a minimal ASGI app with the real route shapes and asserts the executor-built URL delivers the exact original value as the path parameter, for at least a variant with each of the four separators, a region, a gene symbol with punctuation, and a dotted dataset id.

title: SDK: int(limit_sql) re-parses a SQL token and would raise uncaught if a range floor is dropped
description:
Found in the re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 on 2026-08-07. LATENT - not reachable today. Filed rather than fixed in-cycle.

executor.py:974, 1130, 1203, 1294, 1364 each do:
    limit = int(limit_sql)

That silently assumes _token() returned a BARE integer string - which is exactly the assumption _token exists to break. sql_safety._token() parenthesises NEGATIVE values (e.g. '(-5)') so that a leading minus can never render as a SQL line comment in an expression like 'g.gstart - {window_sql}'.

Safe today only because every one of those five call sites passes minimum=1 to sql_int, so a negative can never be produced. If a future call site drops that floor, int('(-5)') raises ValueError - and the enclosing 'except SqlValueError' at executor.py:981 does NOT catch ValueError, so it escapes as an unhandled exception rather than the intended {'success': False, 'error': ...}.

Verified: int(sql_int(-5, name='x')) -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '(-5)'

FIX: stop round-tripping the value through its SQL rendering. Either keep the validated int the caller passed and use that for max_rows, or have sql_int return both the token and the number (the fix agent considered a (token, number) tuple and chose not to). Do not parse the SQL token back into a number.

title: analyze_conversations opens the live chat DB read-write on a shared RWO PVC

title: analyze_conversations: judge input sorts on created_at alone, so ties can invert a turn
description:
Found reviewing genetics-results-suite-4h6.2/.3, deliberately NOT fixed in-cycle.

_format_conversation_for_eval (scripts/analyze_conversations.py ~700-702) still does .sort('created_at') with no tiebreak. created_at has one-second resolution, so a user turn and its own reply can share a timestamp and be presented to the LLM judge in the wrong order.

.2/.3 added message_sort_keys() -> ['created_at', '_rowid'] and applied it to the export path, but deliberately did NOT apply it here, because changing judge INPUT changes judge OUTPUT and would warrant an ANALYZER_VERSION bump - forcing a full Opus-5 re-judge of every conversation at real API cost.

title: chat_turn_metrics: session_id is client-supplied and unvalidated
description:
Found by re-review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.1 on 2026-08-07. NOT blocking - filed rather than fixed in-cycle.

The user_id guard added in .1 stops user B overwriting user A's metrics row. But session_id on the same write path is still client-supplied and never checked for ownership, so:

1. B can INSERT new chat_turn_metrics rows tagged with A's session_id, poisoning per-session cost attribution.
2. delete_session's first DELETE clause is 'session_id = ?' with no user scope on the metrics rows themselves (it is gated on the ownership-scoped chat_sessions delete succeeding, so A must own the session - but any row carrying that session_id is removed regardless of who wrote it). Reproduced: B recorded a row with A's session id; A deleting that session deleted B's row.

Impact today is contained: get_turn_metrics has NO production caller (tests only), so nothing reads these rows yet. It becomes real the moment per-session cost aggregation ships - which is exactly what genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 (the benchmark) intends to do.

Requires the attacker to volunteer their own row, so this is telemetry pollution and self-inflicted loss, not disclosure.

Fix when a reader ships: scope the metrics DELETE by user_id as well as session_id, and validate on write that the session_id belongs to the authenticated user (or drop session_id from the write path and derive it at read time from message_id).

File: src/genetics_mcp_server/db/chat_history_db.py ~437-444 (delete) and the record_turn_metrics call path.

title: _validate_latest_message does not bound assistant-role or replayed message length
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-uog. PRE-EXISTING, weaker than the bug it was found beside.

genetics-mcp-server chat_api.py:90 _validate_latest_message inspects only the newest role == 'user' message, so a client-sent ASSISTANT-role message is length-unbounded, as is any older user turn in replayed history.

The system-role variant of this gap is now closed - uog constrained ChatMessage.role to Literal['user','assistant'], so a system-role message cannot exist in the request at all and there is nothing unbounded for the check to miss.

What remains is a general request-size concern rather than an authority one: a forged assistant turn carries no system authority, and the Anthropic path's _sanitize_tool_blocks / _strip_tool_use_markers already touch those messages. Worth bounding total request size or per-message length regardless.
close_reason:
Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 904284f. Added _validate_request_size: total text across ALL messages (MAX_REQUEST_CHARS, default 2M) and message count (MAX_MESSAGES_PER_REQUEST, default 500), 413 before any model call.

Deliberately NOT the tighter rule of applying max_message_chars to every message: replayed tool results are routinely larger than any typed message, so that would reject ordinary long conversations. A test pins that a 40-turn conversation with 20KB tool results per turn still passes.

Inline image data is excluded from the text budget - images are bounded by max_attachments_per_message, and counting their base64 would reject ordinary image use. Test covers that too.

title: the OpenAI provider branch silently drops user instructions
description:
Found reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.8. Matches that task's stated Anthropic-only scope, so not a defect in it.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py:471 forwards user_instructions only to _stream_anthropic. The OpenAI branch ignores it with no log line.

Consequence: a user who has an instruction set selected and whose request routes to the OpenAI provider gets their instructions dropped invisibly - the UI shows a set applied, the model never sees it. The docstring does say Anthropic-only, but nothing surfaces it at runtime.

Options: implement the equivalent for the OpenAI path, or log once per turn when instructions are dropped, or surface it in the UI. At minimum it should not be silent.

Implemented rather than logged: the UI showed the set applied, so a log line would have left the user misinformed. _stream_openai now takes user_instructions and concatenates it after system_prompt into one system message - the two-block split exists to give each half its own prompt-cache breakpoint, which the OpenAI path has no equivalent for. Order matches Anthropic's. Six tests in TestOpenAIUserInstructions, including one pinning the DISPATCH (that is where the drop was, not in _stream_openai). Docs corrected: project-spec.md said the branch silently drops them.

title: INTERNAL_API_SECRET has four independent reads, two snapshotted at import
description:
Same defect class as genetics-results-suite-pol, different variable. Out of pol's stated scope.

genetics-mcp-server reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET in four places:
- auth/dependencies.py:13 — import-time snapshot
- routers/api_tokens.py:18 — import-time snapshot
- tools/executor.py:108 — live per call
- mcp_server.py:245 — live per call

The import-time snapshots run before load_dotenv() in some import orders, so a value set only in .env is silently ignored there. Fail-closed today: an empty secret skips the bearer branch and falls through to requiring the IAP header, so it is not a hole — but it is the same test trap pol removed, and the four reads can disagree.

Fix: add Settings.internal_api_secret and route all four through it.
close_reason:
Fixed in genetics-mcp-server 6bac696, documented in 14988a7. Added Settings.internal_api_secret and routed all four readers through it: auth/dependencies.py and routers/api_tokens.py (were import-time snapshots, module globals now gone rather than aliased), tools/executor.py and mcp_server.py (were live os.environ reads). Hoisted to a single local import + one settings instance at the top of __init__.

Coverage: nothing in tests/ referenced INTERNAL_API_SECRET at all, so the four could have disagreed silently. New tests/test_internal_api_secret.py covers all four consumers plus the fail-closed empty-secret behaviour; every case sets the env AFTER import, which is what a snapshot cannot see. Mutation-checked: reintroducing the module-global snapshot in dependencies.py fails test_auth_dependency_accepts_the_bearer_form.

Note /chat/v1/auth is @is_public and reports status rather than gating - it answers 200 whatever is presented. The gated route is /chat/v1/me; a test aimed at /auth would prove nothing.

title: batch: correct inaccurate comments and close small coverage gaps in the chat backend
description:

Skew is always in the safe direction (client can only be more restrictive) but the 'shorten by N characters' number can be wrong. Worth a comment at minimum.

FROM .18/.19 REVIEW (browser repo, both non-blocking, left unfixed):

LLMChat.tsx - the two instruction-set fetches run in parallel, so if a SECOND TAB creates and selects a set between the list response and the settings response, this tab sees list=[] / selected=X and clears a valid pointer. Reading the setting first and the list second makes the list provably no-older than the pointer. Costs one serialized round trip.

title: admin feedback timestamps gained a +00:00 suffix — check the browser admin UI
description:
Consequence of genetics-results-suite-ni9 (commit 47c59ca). NOT a defect, but user-visible and unverified on the client.

GET /chat/v1/admin/feedback now emits created_at and latest_at with a +00:00 suffix where session_comment items previously had none. The values were always UTC; only the rendering changed.

Check genetics-results-browser/src/features/admin/adminApi.ts:201, which consumes latest_at - confirm it is not string-compared against a stored value, since a format change would fire one spurious 'new feedback' signal on first load after deploy.

With the +00:00 suffix JS parses as UTC and renders local, which is CORRECT; the bare form was parsed as local, i.e. UTC values were being shown as if local. The change is a fix and the only visible effect is the shift the bead predicted.

title: REQUIRE_AUTH has two sources of truth in the chat backend
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-8r4. PRE-EXISTING, not a production bug, but a live test trap.

genetics-mcp-server reads REQUIRE_AUTH twice:
- src/genetics_mcp_server/auth/dependencies.py:14 snapshots it at IMPORT time into the module global _require_auth, used by auth_required and admin_required.
- src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:260 re-reads os.environ['REQUIRE_AUTH'] per request.

Safe in production: nothing in src/ writes os.environ at runtime (verified — no assignment, setdefault, putenv or update anywhere), and in k8s the value is fixed for the process lifetime, so the two always agree.

The problem is in tests: patch('...dependencies._require_auth', True) moves one and not the other, while patch.dict(os.environ, {'REQUIRE_AUTH': 'true'}) moves the other and not the one. So /chat/v1/auth's is_admin can disagree with admin_required's gate under test — exactly the class of test-isolation trap 8r4 was about.

Fix: route both through settings rather than reading os.environ in two places.

Also worth knowing: seeds quoted in bug reports are only meaningful while pytest-randomly stays pinned at the version 8r4 set. Bumping it resets that history.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 47c59ca (batched — three small fixes in one repo, one cycle). Suite 850 passed / 74 deselected, green on seeds 12345 and 20260804. title: admin feedback pagination can duplicate or skip an item on a same-second tie
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-s5y.5. PRE-EXISTING, out of that task's scope.

genetics-mcp-server routers/admin.py:269 merges list_all_user_comments() with session comments, Python-stable-sorts by created_at, then slices items[offset:offset+limit].

created_at is CURRENT_TIMESTAMP with one-second resolution, so two submissions in the same second tie. The input order from the DB is unconstrained (ORDER BY created_at DESC with no id tiebreak), so the page boundary can shift between requests — an admin paging through feedback can see one item twice or miss one entirely.

This is the same root cause as s5y.5 but a different symptom: no single 'current value' is derived, so s5y.5 deliberately left the comment listings alone. The fix is the same shape — add an id tiebreak to the ORDER BY in get_user_comments / list_all_user_comments, and make the merge sort key (created_at, id).
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit e636200 (shared with 2cl). Verified across all 40,320 permutations of an 8-row input spanning both sources: exactly one merged order, every item appearing exactly once when walking pages with the input reshuffled between requests. HEAD reproduced the reported symptom exactly (one item twice, another never).

A BUG WAS INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the first fix stringified the comment id for tuple homogeneity, which sorts lexicographically — ids 8,9,10,11 rendered as 9,8,11,10, exactly negating the ORDER BY the same fix added. The stringification was also unnecessary: 'source' is compared first, so an int id is never compared against a session uuid. Raw ids now, with the source discriminator proven load-bearing by mutation (dropping it raises TypeError).

Recorded reason corrected: the earlier claim that making the user-comment reads timezone-aware would break this merge key was tested and found FALSE — the key stays total and identically ordered because both stamps render as a fixed 19-char prefix. The decision not to touch them stands on scope grounds only; genetics-results-suite-ni9 owns them.
